text: In 1937, renowned fashion designer Elsa Schiaparelli unveiled one of her most famous creations: a black
ipa: /ɪn 1937 ɹɪnˈaʊnd fˈæʃən dɪzˈaɪnɚ ˈɛlsə schiaparelli ənvˈeɪld wˈʌn ˈʌv hˈɝ mˈoʊst fˈeɪməs kɹiˈeɪʃənz ə blˈæk/
vi: Vào năm 1937, nhà thiết kế thời trang nổi tiếng Elsa Schiaparelli đã giới thiệu một trong những sáng tạo nổi tiếng nhất của bà: một chiếc váy đen

text: stiletto with a pink heel.
ipa: /stəlˈɛtoʊ wˈɪð ə pˈɪŋk hˈil/
vi: giày cao gót mũi nhọn gót hồng.

text: What made this seemingly ordinary piece so noteworthy
ipa: /wˈʌt mˈeɪd ðˈɪs sˈimɪŋli ˈɔɹdənˌɛɹi pˈis sˈoʊ nˈoʊtwˌɝði/
vi: Điều gì đã làm cho tác phẩm tưởng chừng như bình thường này trở nên đáng chú ý như vậy

text: was that it was designed to sit on top of a woman’s head.
ipa: /wˈɑz ðˈæt ˈɪt wˈɑz dɪzˈaɪnd tˈu sˈɪt ˈɑn tˈɑp ˈʌv ə womans hˈɛd/
vi: là nó được thiết kế để đội trên đầu phụ nữ.

text: Created in collaboration with Salvador Dalí, Schiaparelli’s bizarre shoe hat was celebrated
ipa: /kɹiˈeɪtəd ɪn kəlˌæbɚˈeɪʃən wˈɪð sˈælvədˌɔɹ dˈæl schiaparellis bəzˈɑɹ ʃˈu hˈæt wˈɑz sˈɛləbɹˌeɪtɪd/

text: as an iconic contribution to the Surrealist art movement.
ipa: /ˈæz ˈæn ˌaɪkˈɑnɪk kˌɑntɹəbjˈuʃən tˈu ðə surrealist ˈɑɹt mˈuvmənt/

text: Humans have been fashioning caps since the dawn of civilization.
ipa: /hjˈumənz hˈæv bˈɪn fˈæʃənɪŋ kˈæps sˈɪns ðə dˈɔn ˈʌv sˌɪvəlɪzˈeɪʃən/

text: A simple bearskin cap from the Bronze Age is one of the earliest surviving hats, discovered
ipa: /ə sˈɪmpəl bearskin kˈæp fɹˈʌm ðə bɹˈɑnz ˈeɪdʒ ˈɪz wˈʌn ˈʌv ðə ˈɝliəst sɚvˈaɪvɪŋ hˈæts dɪskˈʌvɚd/

text: in the Alps alongside Europe’s oldest mummy, Ötzi the Iceman.
ipa: /ɪn ðə ˈælps əlˈɔŋsˈaɪd europes ˈoʊldəst mˈʌmi tzi ðə ˈaɪsmæn/

text: But we’ve found images of hats that are much older: some believe
ipa: /bˈʌt weve fˈaʊnd ˈɪmədʒəz ˈʌv hˈæts ðˈæt ˈɑɹ mˈʌtʃ ˈoʊldɚ sˈʌm bɪlˈiv/

text: that the “Venus of Willendorf,” a Paleolithic figurine made around 30,000 years ago, is the earliest
ipa: /ðˈæt ðə vˈinəs ˈʌv willendorf ə paleolithic fˌɪɡjɚˈin mˈeɪd ɚˈaʊnd 30000 jˈɪɹz əɡˈoʊ ˈɪz ðə ˈɝliəst/

text: known depiction of woven headgear.
ipa: /nˈoʊn dɪpˈɪkʃən ˈʌv wˈoʊvən hˈɛdɡˌɪɹ/

text: Hats aren’t just for keeping heads warm; they can also be used to make political statements.
ipa: /hˈæts ˈɑɹənt dʒˈʌst fˈɔɹ kˈipɪŋ hˈɛdz wˈɔɹm ðˈeɪ kˈæn ˈɔlsoʊ bˈi jˈuzd tˈu mˈeɪk pəlˈɪtəkəl stˈeɪtmənts/

text: Take the pileus cap, a favorite among ancient Romans and Greeks.
ipa: /tˈeɪk ðə pileus kˈæp ə fˈeɪvɚɪt əmˈʌŋ ˈeɪntʃənt ɹˈoʊmənz ənd ɡɹˈiks/

text: In the Roman Republic, pileus caps were given to previously enslaved people
ipa: /ɪn ðə ɹˈoʊmən ɹipˈʌblək pileus kˈæps wˈɝ ɡˈɪvən tˈu pɹˈiviəsli ɛnslˈeɪvd pˈipəl/

text: as a public sign of their freedom and came to symbolize the ideals
ipa: /ˈæz ə pˈʌblɪk sˈaɪn ˈʌv ðˈɛɹ fɹˈidəm ənd kˈeɪm tˈu sˈɪmbəlˌaɪz ðə aɪdˈilz/

text: of personal and political liberty.
ipa: /ˈʌv pˈɝsɪnəl ənd pəlˈɪtəkəl lˈɪbɚtˌi/

text: In the 18th century, American and French revolutionaries seemed to have conflated the pileus
ipa: /ɪn ðə 18th sˈɛntʃɚi əmˈɛɹəkən ənd fɹˈɛntʃ ɹˌɛvəlˈuʃənˌɛɹiz sˈimd tˈu hˈæv conflated ðə pileus/

text: with the very similar-looking Phrygian cap, embracing the Phrygian as an emblem of their cause.
ipa: /wˈɪð ðə vˈɛɹi similarlooking fɹˈɪdʒiən kˈæp ɛmbɹˈeɪsɪŋ ðə fɹˈɪdʒiən ˈæz ˈæn ˈɛmbləm ˈʌv ðˈɛɹ kˈɑz/

text: This is reflected in renderings of Marianne, a personification of the French Republic,
ipa: /ðˈɪs ˈɪz ɹɪflˈɛktɪd ɪn ɹˈɛndɚɪŋz ˈʌv mˌɛɹiˈæn ə pɚsˌɑnəfəkˈeɪʃən ˈʌv ðə fɹˈɛntʃ ɹipˈʌblək/

text: who often wears a red Phrygian.
ipa: /hˈu ˈɔfən wˈɛɹz ə ɹˈɛd fɹˈɪdʒiən/

text: Hats have also been an essential accessory for projecting status and power.
ipa: /hˈæts hˈæv ˈɔlsoʊ bˈɪn ˈæn ɛsˈɛn��əl æksˈɛsɚi fˈɔɹ pɹədʒˈɛktɪŋ stˈætəs ənd pˈaʊɚ/

text: In Western Europe in the 15th century, nothing conveyed royal excess quite like the hennin.
ipa: /ɪn wˈɛstɚn jˈʊɹəp ɪn ðə 15th sˈɛntʃɚi nˈʌθɪŋ kənvˈeɪd ɹˈɔɪəl ˈɛksˌɛs kwˈaɪt lˈaɪk ðə hennin/

text: Popular among the women of the Burgundy Court, these bejeweled headdresses were crafted from expensive silks
ipa: /pˈɑpjəlɚ əmˈʌŋ ðə wˈɪmən ˈʌv ðə bˈɝɡəndi kˈɔɹt ðˈiz bejeweled hˈɛddɹˌɛsəz wˈɝ kɹˈæftɪd fɹˈʌm ɪkspˈɛnsɪv sˈɪlks/

text: and included variations like a flat-topped design and the daring double-coned escoffion.
ipa: /ənd ˌɪnklˈudəd vˌɛɹiˈeɪʃənz lˈaɪk ə flattopped dɪzˈaɪn ənd ðə dˈɛɹɪŋ doubleconed escoffion/

text: Hat height was restricted according to social rank:
ipa: /hˈæt hˈaɪt wˈɑz ɹistɹˈɪktəd əkˈɔɹdɪŋ tˈu sˈoʊʃəl ɹˈæŋk/

text: while princesses could sport meter-high hennins, noblewomen were limited to much shorter styles.
ipa: /wˈaɪl pɹˈɪnsɛsɪz kˈʊd spˈɔɹt meterhigh hennins noblewomen wˈɝ lˈɪmətəd tˈu mˈʌtʃ ʃˈɔɹtɚ stˈaɪlz/

text: And they weren’t without their critics; hennins were often targeted by clerics
ipa: /ənd ðˈeɪ werent wɪθˈaʊt ðˈɛɹ kɹˈɪtɪks hennins wˈɝ ˈɔfən tˈɑɹɡətɪd bˈaɪ klˈɛɹɪks/

text: and moralists who found their flashy designs impious.
ipa: /ənd mˈɔɹəlˌɪsts hˈu fˈaʊnd ðˈɛɹ flˈæʃi dɪzˈaɪnz ˌɪmpˈaɪəs/

text: Nearly a century later, Suleiman the Magnificent, the longest-reigning sultan of the Ottoman Empire, became known
ipa: /nˈɪɹli ə sˈɛntʃɚi lˈeɪtɚ suleiman ðə mæɡnˈɪfəsənt ðə longestreigning sˈʌltən ˈʌv ðə ˈɑtəmən ˈɛmpaɪɚ bɪkˈeɪm nˈoʊn/

text: for his bold military campaigns and even more audacious headgear.
ipa: /fˈɔɹ hˈɪz bˈoʊld mˈɪlətˌɛɹi kæmpˈeɪnz ənd ˈivɪn mˈɔɹ ɑdˈeɪʃəs hˈɛdɡˌɪɹ/

text: His grand bulb-shaped turbans were adorned with sparkling sprays of diamonds or feathers.
ipa: /hˈɪz ɡɹˈænd bulbshaped tˈɝbənz wˈɝ ədˈɔɹnd wˈɪð spˈɑɹklɪŋ spɹˈeɪz ˈʌv dˈaɪməndz ˈɔɹ fˈɛðɚz/

text: His collection also included a grand four-tiered golden helmet,
ipa: /hˈɪz kəlˈɛkʃən ˈɔlsoʊ ˌɪnklˈudəd ə ɡɹˈænd fourtiered ɡˈoʊldən hˈɛlmət/

text: though some historians suspect it wasn’t actually designed for wearing.
ipa: /ðˈoʊ sˈʌm hɪstˈɔɹiənz səspˈɛkt ˈɪt wasnt ˈæktʃˌuəli dɪzˈaɪnd fˈɔɹ wˈɛɹɪŋ/

text: Rather, the crown was crafted to flaunt his immense power and wealth to his rivals.
ipa: /ɹˈæðɚ ðə kɹˈaʊn wˈɑz kɹˈæftɪd tˈu flˈɔnt hˈɪz ˌɪmˈɛns pˈaʊɚ ənd wˈɛlθ tˈu hˈɪz ɹˈaɪvəlz/

text: For other caps, the real story lies in their making.
ipa: /fˈɔɹ ˈʌðɚ kˈæps ðə ɹˈil stˈɔɹi lˈaɪz ɪn ðˈɛɹ mˈeɪkɪŋ/

text: The sleek British top hat was first introduced in the early 19th century
ipa: /ðə slˈik bɹˈɪtɪʃ tˈɑp hˈæt wˈɑz fˈɝst ˌɪntɹədˈust ɪn ðə ˈɝli 19th sˈɛntʃɚi/

text: as powdered wigs fell out of fashion.
ipa: /ˈæz pˈaʊdɚd wˈɪɡz fˈɛl ˈaʊt ˈʌv fˈæʃən/

text: Originally crafted from the fur of animals like beavers, hat makers would soak the material
ipa: /ɚˈɪdʒənəli kɹˈæftɪd fɹˈʌm ðə fˈɝ ˈʌv ˈænəməlz lˈaɪk bˈivɚz hˈæt mˈeɪkɚz wˈʊd sˈoʊk ðə mətˈɪɹiəl/

text: in vats filled with toxic mercuric nitrate to improve the felts quality and density.
ipa: /ɪn vˈæts fˈɪld wˈɪð tˈɑksɪk mɚkjˈʊɹɪk nˈaɪtɹˌeɪt tˈu ˌɪmpɹˈuv ðə fˈɛlts kwˈɑləti ənd dˈɛnsəti/

text: But prolonged exposure to the chemical in poorly ventilated spaces led many hatters to develop mercury
ipa: /bˈʌt pɹəlˈɔŋd ɪkspˈoʊʒɚ tˈu ðə kˈɛməkəl ɪn pˈuɹli vˈɛntəlˌeɪtɪd spˈeɪsəz lˈɛd mˈɛni hatters tˈu dɪvˈɛləp mˈɝkjɚi/

text: poisoning, suffering symptoms like irritability, slurred speech, memory problems, and tremors.
ipa: /pˈɔɪzənɪŋ sˈʌfɚɪŋ sˈɪmptəmz lˈaɪk ˌɪɹɪtəbˈɪləti slˈɝd spˈitʃ mˈɛmɚi pɹˈɑbləmz ənd tɹˈɛmɚz/

text: The figure of the Mad Hatter, immortalized in Lewis Carroll’s “Alice in Wonderland,” is a popular
ipa: /ðə fˈɪɡjɚ ˈʌv ðə mˈæd hˈætɚ ˌɪmˈɔɹtəlaɪzd ɪn lˈuɪs carrolls ˈæləs ɪn wˈʌndɚlˌænd ˈɪz ə pˈɑpjəlɚ/

text: reference to this devastating plight.
ipa: /ɹˈɛfɚəns tˈu ðˈɪs dˈɛvəstˌeɪtɪŋ plˈaɪt/

text: Thankfully, in the late 1800s, as more people became aware of the dangers of mercury, many
ipa: /θˈæŋkfəli ɪn ðə lˈeɪt 1800s ˈæz mˈɔɹ pˈipəl bɪkˈeɪm əwˈɛɹ ˈʌv ðə dˈeɪndʒɚz ˈʌv mˈɝkjɚi mˈɛni/

text: countries began to ban its use.
ipa: /kˈʌntɹiz bɪɡˈæn tˈu bˈæn ˈɪts jˈus/

text: Over the following century, top hats, bowlers, and bonnets largely fell out of fashion
ipa: /ˈoʊvɚ ðə fˈɑloʊɪŋ sˈɛntʃɚi tˈɑp hˈæts bˈoʊlɚz ��nd bonnets lˈɑɹdʒli fˈɛl ˈaʊt ˈʌv fˈæʃən/

text: as everyday wear, but one cap proves that hats are still big business: the baseball cap.
ipa: /ˈæz ˈɛvɹidˈeɪ wˈɛɹ bˈʌt wˈʌn kˈæp pɹˈuvz ðˈæt hˈæts ˈɑɹ stˈɪl bˈɪɡ bˈɪznəs ðə bˈeɪsbˈɔl kˈæp/

text: What began as a practical part of a baseball uniform stepped off the field
ipa: /wˈʌt bɪɡˈæn ˈæz ə pɹˈæktəkəl pˈɑɹt ˈʌv ə bˈeɪsbˈɔl jˈunəfˌɔɹm stˈɛpt ˈɔf ðə fˈild/

text: and onto the streets in the 1960s.
ipa: /ənd ˈɑntu ðə stɹˈits ɪn ðə 1960s/

text: The cap’s cost-effective, adjustable design, along with its easy integration of logos, badges,
ipa: /ðə kˈæps costeffective ədʒˈʌstəbəl dɪzˈaɪn əlˈɔŋ wˈɪð ˈɪts ˈizi ˌɪntəɡɹˈeɪʃən ˈʌv lˈoʊɡˌoʊz bˈædʒɪz/

text: and trademarks, has driven its mass commercialization.
ipa: /ənd tɹˈeɪdmˌɑɹks hˈæz dɹˈɪvən ˈɪts mˈæs kəmˌɝʃəlɪzˈeɪʃən/

text: In the United States, some estimate that baseball caps alone make up around 80%
ipa: /ɪn ðə junˈaɪtɪd stˈeɪts sˈʌm ˈɛstəmət ðˈæt bˈeɪsbˈɔl kˈæps əlˈoʊn mˈeɪk ˈʌp ɚˈaʊnd 80/

text: of the entire hat market.
ipa: /ˈʌv ðə ɪntˈaɪɚ hˈæt mˈɑɹkət/

text: But as for the future, who knows what type of hat will capture our hearts—
ipa: /bˈʌt ˈæz fˈɔɹ ðə fjˈutʃɚ hˈu nˈoʊz wˈʌt tˈaɪp ˈʌv hˈæt wˈɪl kˈæptʃɚ ˈaʊɚ hˈɑɹts/

text: and our heads— next.
ipa: /ənd ˈaʊɚ hˈɛdz nˈɛkst/
